notes.title: Ginormous 1.7 Beta Update
notes.content:
I have just updated the beta again, this time to version 1.7.  

It's getting much closer to the official 2.0 version, which I hope to have ready before the end of the year.  There are a lot of things to talk about with this update, so let's start with the biggest features.

[h1]New Main Menu[/h1]
[list]
[*] The Main Menu looks exactly the same, but the functionality has been updated significantly
[*] Now you can access the main menu while you are playing the game, it no longer restarts the game
[*] From the main menu, you can start a new game, or load a different saved game
[*] Note, if you try to start a new game or load an old game, you will still lose your current progress
[*] There is a warning that will appear before you do this, so pay attention
[*] If you are in your ship, you can always save the game before doing these things
[/list]


[h1]Video Options[/h1]
[list]
[*] The new video options panel does actually require you to restart the engine after you make changes
[*] This is to (hopefully) prevent some of the graphics and video problems people were facing with the old version
[*] Note: It is still recommended to play Star Explorers at the default 1280 x 720 resolution if possible  
[*] If that's not possible on your monitor, try to keep the width at 1280, and adjust the height to match one of your monitor's available sizes
[/list]


[h1]Star Chart[/h1]
[list]
[*] The Star Chart has had a big overhaul
[*] It looks pretty much the same as before, but a lot of the functionality has been updated
[*] You should no longer experience the shaking camera when zooming in and out with the scroll wheel
[*] Hovering over sectors, stars, planets and other clickable objects will cause the mouse cursor to turn red, just like in your spaceship viewport
[*] There was a problem when the camera was low and a different sector appeared behind stars or planets, causing them to be un-clickable, that should be resolved now
[*] Clicking on "Planets" with the mothership selected caused planets to appear around the mothership (in the chart only) this should no longer occur
[/list]


[h1]Flex Suit Upgrade[/h1]
[list]
[*] The flex suit is available only as a blueprint for those daring explorers who are determined enough to find it
[*] This flex suit originally allowed the player to move unhindered underwater
[*] It still has this feature, but it is also a much more powerful suit overall
[/list]


[h1]Bug Fixes and Other Improvements[/h1]
[list]
[*] Alien spaceships on planets used to sometimes intersect with the larger landscape objects, causing aliens and their cache boxes to appear inside of the larger rocks or trees - this should no longer happen
[*] Keys for ancient ruins were somehow always "Emerald" - now different kinds of keys should be available 
[*] Sizes of items dropped have been fixed
[*] Selling space suits will now get you some cash, previously space suits displayed a selling price, but did not actually increase the player's money when sold
[*] Storage caches are now saved at the time a planet or cave is loaded, previously these were only saved when leaving a location, so if you died or the game was shut down, those caches and their items would be gone the next time you visited
[*] Transferring items to your ship's storage should now update the amount in storage (it actually just causes the detail panel to disappear, but when you click it the quantity should be updated)
[*] Closing an alert panel with weapon drawn should no longer cause your weapon to fire
[*] Your ship can now only be repaired while you are aboard
[*] A big terrain bug was fixed, but it would only have effected players who changed their "max terrain size" to lower than 14
[*] A game crashing bug was fixed when enamy UFOs were present and player warped to another system
[*] Another game crashing bug was fixed when asteroids were destroyed, but player did not pick up the space ore before warping to another system
[*] Planet textures are now purged during every warp, preventing RAM from being over-used, along with random crashes that may have occurred as a result (Note this would only effect players who warped to multimple systems without ever landing on a planet, as landing on a planet would also purge all the planet textures)
[*] The close button on the trade dialogue with aliens now works
[/list]

Also, don't forget to vote for Star Explorers for Indie of the Year on IndieDB!
https://www.indiedb.com/games/star-explorers

notes.title: Happy Thanksgiving! and Update 1.6 in Beta
notes.content:
I have uploaded the latest version of Star Explorers to Beta test.  Again, if you want to try it, choose "Star Explorers > Properties > Betas" then select "beta" from the drop down menu.

[h1]Bugs Fixed[/h1][list]
[*]Sorry about this, but the last version (1.5) actually introduced a few bugs
[*]I fixed the reloading caves bug that came with the last version (1.5) and you should now be able to re-enter caves that you've visited
[*]I fixed a problem with caches on planet surfaces that was also introduced in version 1.5
[/list]
[h1]New Features[/h1][list]
[*]Not so much a feature as an optimization, I have reconfigured the terrain generator and terrain reloaders to work faster and more efficiently
[*]When you first land on a planet, the terrain generator now selects from a set of pre-generated terrain files.  
[*]These terrain files were procedurally generated in advance, so the program no longer has to generate them while you're playing.  
[*]This serves to speed up the loading process, and will eliminate the potential for errors in terrain generation that caused planets to have to restart.  
[*]I've also optimized the terrain re-loading function, so it is much faster than before.  
[*]Now if you leave a planet, or enter a cave, it only takes a few seconds to re-load that terrain when you return.  
[*]So far I have not encountered any errors with these new features, and they seem to work as planned.
[/list]
[h1]Next Steps[/h1][list]
[*]I noticed some problems (again introduced with version 1.5) that causes the wrong types of items to appear in certain caches.  This will be addressed in the next update.
[*]Access to the main menu currently requires the game to restart.  This was always a temporary solution to a certain problem I faced, but it's time to get to fixing it.
[*]For some reason, ancient ruins are always and only requiring emerald keys, where there are supposed to be a number of different key types.  
[*]I plan to fine-tune some aspects of the enemy spaceship interiors, and I want to include friendly spaceships too.  
[/list]
There are a lot more features and fixes I want to attend to, but these are the ones I plan to work on for the next update.  As always, if you have questions or find problems with the game, don't hesitate to write about them in the Bug Report, on the discussions forum.

Finally, there is turkey to be had, and I must go for now.  Have a great holiday!

notes.title: Nomination for Star Explorers and Update
notes.content:
I don't want to overstep here, but I would just like to mention that Steam is allowing players to nominate games for awards right now.  I know Star Explorers is not a run-away hit (as I've mentioned many times) but I do believe it qualifies as a "Labor of Love" going on nearly six years of development.  

A few button clicks from you lovely people could make a huge difference in this overly ambitious project.  

I also will remind everyone that a nice review is always welcome, in case you were feeling extra generous :)  

Update:
Regarding the terrain generation issue, I've timed the process for an average sized planet (14 x 14 grid) with life on it.  Here are the results so far:

Old Method:  Generating - 60 seconds
                      Reloading  - 49 seconds

New Method: Generating - 45 seconds
                      Reloading   - 13 seconds (!)

This is a vast improvement, especially when it comes to going in and out of caves and ancient ruins.  Also, the initial generation of planets was fraught with uncertainty, and it could actually have to restart when a particuar terrain was not working.  It could sometimes take well over a minute or two.

Nevertheless, I believe I can cut down on that 45 seconds with some other improvements.  I will let you know what happens.

notes.title: Version 1.5 in Beta
notes.content:
I have uploaded the latest version of Star Explorers to the "beta" version.  If you are interested in helping to test out the latest features, you can activate it by going to "Star Explorers > Properties > Betas" and choose "beta" from the drop down menu.  It should queue an update the next time you play.  

You'll know it worked if you see "Version 1.5" on the loading screen.  Please note, this has not been thoroughly tested, so it may have some bugs still.  Consider it like an extended Early Access period for Verison 2.0 which will be the next official release.  

Here's what you can expect in this latest version of Star Explorers:

[h1]Your Spaceship[/h1]
[list]
[*]Your ship is now armed with laser cannons.  To shoot, first you must enter "Combat Mode" by hitting the space bar while you are flying the spaceship.
[*]Your ship may also take damage and be destroyed, so be careful out there!
[*]If your ship does take damage, fear not, there are new ship repair kits available.  Find them or purchase them from traders. They look like health or suit repair kits, but have a yellow highlight.
[/list]

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/28731582/e6deb3d7574f693bcfd8c2d89cf2fd7d14a22452.jpg[/img]
[i]Your landing craft in the hangar of an alien spaceship[/i]

[h1]Enemy Spacecraft[/h1]
[list]
[*]If you see any flying saucers, for now they are all hostile.  Shoot them before they shoot you.  
[*]If you are able to hit one, you will see and hear a green explosion.  This has disabled the ship.  You can continue to shoot it in order to destroy it - OR - you may choose to board it and explore its interior.  
[*]If you do go aboard an alien spaceship, be warned, they are known to have robotic sentries that will show no mercy to intruders!
[/list]

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/28731582/f1ae4b45adb4b1da8c3aa1bb12e1a18f8ee1107d.jpg[/img]
[i]Be careful around these guys[/i]

[h1]Asteroids[/h1]
[list]
[*]Stars now have asteroids orbiting them.  
[*]You may shoot asteroids ... it is fun.
[*]Shooting asteroids may release a bit of floating space debris
[*]If you have room in your ship's storage, you can pick up this debris by simply flying into it.  But don't fly into asteroids, they will damage your ship!
[/list]

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/28731582/d2b3a66b55fa5c2f63bda05fe4d3026d0aac2f71.jpg[/img]
[i]An asteroid up close[/i]

[h1]Improved Item Interaction[/h1]
[list]
[*]I have struggled with this since the beginning, but I think I've finally got it down.
[*]When on a planet or in a cave, you should still see the hand icon pop up when you are facing an object that you can interact with.
[*]Previously, this was somewhat problematic, and it was easy to lose track of items, forcing the player to have to move around in order to detect the item.
[*]I have rewritten this code from scratch, and now it seems much more consistent.  
[*]Let me know how it's working for you!
[*]Picking up items will now play a little "reward" sound.
[*]A different sound plays if your inventory is full.
[/list]

[h1]Other Improvements[/h1]
[list]
[*]The rocket launcher would sometimes cause a terrain tile to temporarily turn black, if the flashlight was active.  This has been addressed.
[/list]

[h1]Next Steps[/h1]
As I've mentioned previously, I want to improve the way the game generates terrain.  It takes too long, and occasionally takes waaaaay too long.  I have an idea on how to improve this, and will be trying it out soon.

The Star Chart is still a but wacky.  I want to streamline all the controls and menu options, so it is easy to use and understand.  

More sounds.  I want to add sounds for menus and other game features, to improve the overall user experience.  

More sapceships.  The current enemy spaceships are just the first step.  I want to also include friendly spaceships that the player can board to interact with the aliens.  

For now that's all ... enjoy the new update!

notes.title: Update Progress and Trading Cards
notes.content:
As I mentioned previously, a major update is underway.  It's taking a bit longer than most updates, because I'm adding a completely new kind of area to explore, and I have to finish all the modelling and coding before I can really start testing it properly.  

With that said, there has been progress, and I have some in-game screenshots to share...

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/28731582/5bc91af7a5394595a729f54a0dd795217cfcc107.jpg[/img]
You will be able to board and explore alien spaceships.

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/28731582/9247968af8979e12836291db147e87807f6e9bff.jpg[/img]
I'm still working on these interiors, and plan to add ship defenses, living aliens and other features before the update is complete.

[h1]Trading Cards[/h1]
I was informed recently that Star Explorers is eligible to get its own set of Steam Trading Cards.  I am working on those, and hope to have them up and running by some time next week.  

[h1]Star Chart and Other Issues[/h1]
In addition to this, I am planning to have a look at the 3D Star Chart, to see if I can smooth out its interactivity.  It seems like it's not responding the way I intended.   If you've had any problems with it, or feel it could be improved, don't hesitate to let me know.  

Another issue that I want to address is allowing players to get back to the main menu without restarting the game.  This is a big one, as it's really something I did not expect to find problems doing.  However, when I load a game without restarting, it causes problems and bugs to arise.  The simplest way to prevent this was to prevent players from loading their games :)  Unfortunatly, that's not a great long term solution and it makes Star Explorers look like it was programmed by an insane person (was it?)

I also plan to have a look at problems with certain screen sizes.  Some players have complained of problems when they switch to certain resolutions.  This is difficult to fix, because it really depends on the monitor being used and other factors I might not have control over.  As always, it's best to play at the native resolution of 1280 x 720, and I've found that windowed mode seems to work better than full screen.  If your monitor does not support this resolution you can set a custom resolution in the Options Panel, but I recommend keeping the width at 1280 (wherever possible) and adjusting the height to match your monitor's limitations.

Finally, I am annoyed by how long it takes to generate planets sometimes.  I have, in the works, a system of making this far less time consuming.  

[h1]Feedback and Reviews[/h1]
As always I am open for feedback and suggestions.  I'm not talking about making Star Explorers into a multiplayer game, or major changes, but if you encounter any problems, or think of ways in which existing elements can be improved, I would love to hear about them.  

Finally, reviews are the best way to reward a developer for their hard work.  I would never ask anyone to write a positive review if they don't genuinely like the game, but I am hoping that maybe some of you who do enjoy Star Explorers or want to help this good project get better, would consider this as a possibility.  

Thanks!  The game would not even exist without your input and interest.  My goal is to one day be able to work on this game, and others, full time, so I appreciate everyone who has helped contribute to that possibility.

notes.title: Stuff is Happening
notes.content:
I don't want to give away too many details yet.  I have had a busy few weeks, and have not been able to put much time into Star Explorers.  However, the last few days have been productive ones, and a new beta version is imminent. 

The update will include, and I am being intentionally vague...

1. Things to do in outer space, other than travelling to and from planets.  

2. These things will involve shooting laser cannons. 

3. They will also involve being able to collect things directly to your ship's storage.  

4. Your ship will be able to take damage as well.

5. And you will be able to repair it.

6.  There are more things I intend to do, but this is everything I have worked on so far.  I prefer not to say anything about those other things until I have something actually working.  

I will probably release a few beta versions while I make these new features, until I have a solid, working update.  Then I can run a new promotion, to see if the new features bring some new players, or inspire older players to pick up the game again.  

As one of the recent reviews mentioned, a lot of people who bought the game only played for a short time.  I do understand this, the game is not the most user friendly.  I am hoping a little more action in space might help to capture people's interests.  Anyway, I still have a wishlist of features that I wanted from the beginning, so I hope to be able to add most of these before I move on to a different project.

notes.title: Game Updated to Version 1.4
notes.content:
The default version of Star Explorers has been updated to 1.4.  

This includes all the new features you can read about in more detail in the previous few announcements. As a summary, here are some of the most important new features:

[h1]New Features[/h1]
[list]
[*]Fixed Major Resolution Bug - this caused brand new games to start at a very low resolution.  It should now start at the default 1280 x 720
[*]Casual Mode - allows you to play a slightly limited version of the game purely for exploration - this is really in a beta form right now and may be tweaked in later updates
[*]Improved Load Game Menu - allows you to choose saved games from a list
[*]3D Star Chart - gives you a visual depiction of sectors, stars and planets along with the location of your spaceship and the mothership
[*]Smart Item Transfer - will automatically assign new items to stack on the same type of item if it already exists in your inventory.  This only works for "stackable" items like ammo, crystals and others
[*]More Resolution Options - including a custom resolution field to allow the game to work on any monitor
[*]Improved Scanning on Spaceship - fixed the strange tendancy for the player to lose focus of interactive objects while aboard the spaceship
[*]New Ship Display - a wider viewscreen and computer console gives the player a better view of the Star Explorers galaxy
[/list]

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/28731582/42d20d437edb7d317895420db7e7c7f577fff891.jpg[/img]
Here is the new and improved screen with a much wider view

I try to test all these things before uploading anything and so far it all seems to work okay.  With that said, as a one man team, it's always possible for me to miss something.  Let me know if you encounter any errors.

notes.title: Update 1.4 Beta
notes.content:
Beta version 1.4 is coming soon!  It addresses a few bugs that somehow got overlooked, and introduces the first attempt at "Casual Mode."

[h1]Resolution Problems[/h1]
[list]
[*]A huge bug existed for players who run Star Explorers for the first time - it seems that the default screen resolution was never properly set, and the game would start at 800 x 600!  One player did point this out, but he had an uncommon monitor resolution, and I thought it was related to that  
[*]Now the game should start at 1280 x 720 as default  
[*]Players who had an existing game prior to the full release would not have encountered this bug, as the game would have looked to their existing settings[/list]

[h1]Improved Scanning in Spaceship[/h1]
[list]
[*]Scanning is the thing that determines whether the little hand icon will show up, allowing you to interact with the ship's console and bay doors
[*]Previously, this was a bit touchy and would not work when you stepped too close to the interactive panel
[*]It should be more robust now, and should not shut off when you get too close[/list]

[h1]Inventory Glitch[/h1]
[list]
[*]A bug in the inventory function prevented (in some cases) the number of an item from increasing if you already possessed that item
[*]This should now work correctly in all cases[/list]

[h1]Casual Mode[/h1]
[list]
[*]Under the Options Menu, there is a small toggle called "Casual Mode"
[*]Clicking this will change certain key aspects of gameplay, here is a summary of what it changes
[*]Fuel is no longer needed to fly the spaceship
[*]Your character will never run out of oxygen
[*]Your character will no longer take any damage
[*]Your ship will no longer be trapped in a star's or planet's gravity well
[*]Your ship will be able to pass through planets and stars
[*]Aliens will be friendly by default (though you may still choose to attack them)
[*]Hostile Aliens will no longer spawn in caves
[*]Floater Aliens may actually be hostile, but should not actually cause damage
[*]With these easements, the game will not be challenging at all, so I have made a few other adjustments as well
[*]Armor upgrades will not appear in caches or at traders
[*]Laser pistols are the only weapons available
[*]Steam Achievements will not work in Casual Mode[/list]

I hope you enjoy these new features.  I will probably be making this version (1.4) into the default version in a few days after I test it some more.  Let me know if you encounter any issues.  Also, if you haven't tried the beta version before, go to Star Explorers>Properties>Betas and choose "beta" from the drop down menu.  

The beta version also included the 3D Star Chart, improvements to inventory, a better Load Game menu and more.  Check the last few updates to see what else is in the beta version.

notes.title: Version 1.3 in Beta
notes.content:
A couple new features have been added to the beta version of Star Explorers.  

[h1]Updated Star Chart- Again[/h1]
The star chart has been updated again, the mothership is now represented on as a green mothership shaped icon.  

[h1]Inventory Overhaul[/h1]
Inventory, trade and cache boxes now have some enhancements.  First, when you take in new inventory, it will check to see if you already have the same type of item, and will add to the existing amount, if the item is stackable.  Okay, yes this functionality already existed, however, there was a problem if there was an empty slot before the existing item.  Now it will check all the slots first, then, only if that item does not exist, will it add the new item to the empty slot.  I hope this makes sense. 

Secondly, an amount slider has been added to all inventory transactions.  Previously you could only choose the amount when selling items.  Now you can choose a specific amount when buying or selling from a trader, and when taking or placing items in a cache.  

[h1]How Are We Doing[/h1]
Star Explorers is improving as a game, and the numbers are reflecting that.  Although it is by no means a run-away success, and sales numbers have fallen dramatically since the first week of it's full release, they are starting to creep upwards again.  Maybe it's too early to call this a trend, but  have not seen that happen with any of my previous games, outside of a sale or some other external marketing effort, so I'll take it as a good sign.

Secondly, the average amount of time users spend playing the game has gone up a lot since its original release back in 2017.  I'll take this as another good sign overall.  Also there is a small but growing core of players who are spending a lot of time in-game.  This trend could explain the increase in sales activity, since other Steam users will be able to see what games people are playing, and may become interested as a result ... so keep playing!

Star Explorers has been described as a slow burner.  It's a bit open ended and maybe a bit bewildering to new players.  But as you get used to the controls, and begin finding your way around the gaaxy, you will be creating new experiences.  The procedural nature of the game will ensure that each play-through will be unique, with it's own challenges and rewards.  I would encourage players to stick with the game, and give it a chance to get interesting before throwing in the towel.  Also, I am still totally open to feedback, so if you have a problem or a suggestion, don't hesitate to contact me, or just open a discussion here on the Community Hub.

[h1]What's Next[/h1]
These positive trends, however slight at this point, are helping me to keep focused on the game.  Improvements will be slow but hopefully steady, until I have depleted all my energies.  The next fixes will include improving the game's interactivity.  Standing a little too close to a console or item sometimes makes the hand icon disappear, I need to improve this.  Also, the current star chart has similar issues when you are attempting to select a star or planet.  Holding the right-mouse button and rotating the view will help in the current state, but I want to make this a better experience as well.  

Casual mode is another aspect I want to work on next.  I've found a number of players feel the game is too hard (including my own kids) and I want to offer an option for those who would just like to explore, without the challenges of survival.  While I like the idea of adding this option, I still would want to encourage players to try the "real" game.  To do this, I think I would have to do something kind of drastic, like disabling inventory.  There would be no need to collect items, materials, upgrades or weapons if there is no survival aspect to the game.  So inventory and trade would not serve any actual purpose, right?  Anyway, just thinking out-loud at this point.  Any feedback is welcome.

Thanks for playing Star Explorers!

notes.title: Beta Update 1.2
notes.content:
A couple new features have been added.  

[h1]New View Screen[/h1]
I widened the viewscreen in the ship to allow the player to see more of the galaxy from the console.  Since I was thinking about updating the interior of the ship, having a wider viewscreen would be the first issue to address.  That probably won't happen for a while though, so for now I added this simple fix.

[h1]Updated Star Chart[/h1]
The star chart has been updated.  Instead of presenting data as a kind of spread sheet, it is not a, interactive 3D Map.  It still displays the exact same data as before, i.e. only sectors, stars and planets that have been scanned, but presents them in 3 dimensions.  

You can still read specific information, change names and take notes as before, and warping to stars is still accessible from the new chart.  In addition, there is a little green pointer that represents your spaceship.  I plan to add the mothership next.

Left click on sectors, stars and planets to access their information.  Right clicking will allow you to rotate the camera, and scrolling with the middle mouse will allow you to zoom in and out.  It still feels a bit clunky, but it is a work in progress.

notes.title: Version 1.1 Ready for Beta Testing

[/list]

[h1]Screen Resolution is Back[/h1]

[*]The new "Custom Resolution" button allows you to meet the needs of any monitor.  This is still in beta so please let me know if it's working or not.
[*]I updated the font in the main spaceship console so it now scales with the screen resolution, I still have to do this with other fonts in future updates
[*]The window border has been removed so you can play in windowed mode at the same resolution as your desktop - previously it would cause an error when switching to the desktop resolution while in windowed mode
[/list]

[h1]Feedback Always Welcome[/h1]
User interface is admitedly not my strongest area, so any feedback is greatly appreciated.  I will be testing this on all the different computers in my house as well.

notes.title: Reviews
notes.content:
So there are some negative reviews coming in, and I will admit some are well deserved.  The biggest issue people are having seems to be with the User Interface and overall logic of the game.  

I am taking notes and coming up with a list of things to improve for the next update.  Here's what I have so far:

[h1]Proposed Fixes and Improvements:[/h1]
[list]
[*]Main Menu should be accessible once game is begun (currently the game restarts to access the main menu after you start playing)
[*]Scanning planets automatically- without having to seek them out visually
[*]Make the star chart more usable/understandable - I think zooming into a selected sector and showing the stars, then zooming into the stars to show the planets, while displaying the relevant data, would be a nice way to approach this
[*]Reintroduce higher resolution options
[*]Reduce load times as much as possible on planets/caves
[*]Improve the interaction "hand" icon, which gets a bit finicky when you move too close to an object
[*]More usefull scanning device that gives locations of surface features, and shows paths in caves (Note: see casual mode below)
[*]Better Inventory System - checking for stackable items - allow moving/rearranging items
[*]Update Manual and In-Game Tutorial
[/list]

[h1]Proposed New Features:[/h1]
[list]
[*]Casual Mode - allowing players to forgo the Story/Survival aspect of the game and simply explore. Perhaps all the ease of use options would be set to on in this mode, but set to off in Survival/Story mode.  Maybe a Hardcore mode would be nice to add also
[*]More detailed spaceship - I have always wanted to add living quarters, more storage, an engine room and the actual hangar where you would board the landing shuttle
[*]Alien Spaceships - with actual space battles as one aspect
[*]Alien Spaceships - to be borded and explored (like caves) - Aliens would still be either friendly or hostile, making each ship a different kind of encounter
[*]Controller support
[/list]

I will be taking some time off before beginning to address all these things.  However, I definitely want to put in at least one more major update before moving on from this game.  I would start with the fixes and improvements, then slowly work into the new features.  

Thoughts?  Ideas?  Suggestions?  I am open to all.  If there is something that you feel the game is missing or perhaps something you don't like about it, don't hesitate to chime in.  

Ideally all of this would have been addressed before the full release, but here we are.

notes.title: Version 1.0 Ready
notes.content:
[h1]Beta Testing Complete[/h1]
Star Explorers is officially no longer in beta testing.  

Does this mean the game is perfect and finished and will never change again?  No.  It is simply the version of the game I described in my design document, and all the major bugs (to the best of my knowledge) have been dealt with.  

As you may notice there is now only one version of the game available.  This is to encourage players to update to the newest version.  It will require starting a new game if you were not playing the most recent beta versions.  Sorry to do this, but I have to ensure as consistent an experience as possible for new players, and I don't want to confuse people who are purchasing the game for the first time.  

I am also, however, a flexible and understanding person.  If you were in the middle of a game, and really really want to continue playing it, let me know and we can figure out how to make it happen.  I could, for instance, create another legacy version for old players, and put a password on it, so no one accidentally installs it.

[h1]Early Access[/h1]
Thanks so much for participating in the Star Explorers Early Access experience!  Without you and all your valuable feedback, I don't think the game would have progressed as far as it has.  To be perfectly honest, part of me wishes I had waited until it was this far before even releasing it, as some of the early bugs ruined many people's experiences with the game.  However, I also feel like I would not have ever been able to find them and fix them on my own, so ultimately Early Access accomplished what it was made for.  And I have all of you to thank … so thanks!

[h1]Re-Installing[/h1]
Due to some Steam related issues, simply updating the game may leave some room for files to not install correctly.  It is strongly recommended that you uninstall the existing version of Star Explorers, restart Steam, then install the new version.  If you do not do this, and you encounter any problems with the game, the first thing I will ask you is whether you uninstalled, then re-installed the game, so don't say I didn't warn you!

This does not mean that the game is 100% bug free, I would be a fool to suggest such a thing.  However, it would be important to isolate actual bugs from issues caused by potential file mix ups.  A Valve employee told me that these things are possible and have happened in the past.  He said the best way to resolve them is to reinstall the game from scratch.  Don't worry, your saved game files should not be touched.  

[h1]NOTE:[/h1] 
You will have to manually delete the “settings.cfg” and “controls.cfg” files.

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/28731582/1b307f46f984d39178d64959e46b9e8abfdcf1e3.jpg[/img]

[h1]The Old-School Pixel Shader[/h1]
I added this feature to the Video Options menu.  Try it out.  The lower resolution and reduced color palette give the game a charming 1990's feel.  Depending on user feedback, I may make it the default shader, but don't worry, in any case all the existing options will remain available.    

[h1]Spreading the Word[/h1]
If you enjoy Star Explorers, please tell people about it.  Maybe it will resonate with other people, you never know, right?  I plan to send out access keys to various game reviewers and YouTubers in the next few days.  Look out for those videos, and let people know about them.  I will try to share any I encounter here on the Community hub.  If anyone knows about marketing games, please feel free to chime in with suggestions.

notes.title: Update 4.6H
notes.content:
Small update that removes the "smoothing" shader I was testing out.  It is still available as an option in the Video Options Panel.  

Note: You cannot use the Smooth Pixel Shader along with the Old School Pixel Shader, it is either one or the other, or neither.  

The Smooth Pixel Shader is an approximation at anti-aliasing.  When I tested actual anti-aliasing in the game engine, it had a bad effect on any transparent sprites and textures.  This is actually a blur effect, but it is reduced to just a small area, so the effect is to smooth out edges.  The drawback is that is also gives the textures a slightly fuzzy appearance.

notes.title: Update 4.6D
notes.content:
I found a couple problems with the previous update, which is why this one is being uploaded now.  I would otherwise have worked on it a bit more...

[h1]Fixed[/h1]
Cave Aliens in 4.6C would crash thanks to my new "improved" breath attack code.  Now they should work properly.

[h1]New Feature[/h1]
Lens Flare - I've been wanting to do this for a while.  There was a previous version in the game's script innactive for a long time, and I finally had another go at it.  
I did experience an error on a couple occasions when using the lens flare.  It messed up the player's movement and was pretty terrible.  I made changes to the script that seem to have fixed this issue.  I would like to have tested it a bit more thoroughly, but I had to update the cave aliens which were definitely broken in the last update.  

Since I could no longer get the lens flare to malfunction I am assuming my changes to the script fixed the problem.  However, please let me know if you encounter an error where moving the mouse will cause your camera to zoom around the level.  Hopefully it won't happen.

[h1]More Bugs[/h1]
I recently discovered that some planets with no atmosphere will not show the sun's disk (or lens flare - which is probably why I noticed it).  I am working on this for the next update.

notes.title: Beta Updated to Version 4.6C
notes.content:
4.6C adds a couple new perks for players.  

[h1]Manual[/h1]
The first thing you might notice is a "Read Manual" button on the main menu, and in the game menu.  Click on it to open a link to the manual.  The manual is also included in the game folder as PDF, in the "Manual" subfolder.

[h1]Forests[/h1]
Forests have been re-introduced.  They really dragged on the frame-rate the last time I tried to introduce more heavily forested planets.  This time, with the updated terrain generator, and the new way in which planet objects are handled, they seem much less challenging for my GPU/CPU.  Forest density will be modified by the overall terrain density setting in the Video Options panel.

[h1]Alien Breath Attacks and Vents[/h1]
Aliens with a ranged breath attack have a better working script now.  They may pose a greater challenge now, but I was able to fight them with the standard pistol and space suit, so nothing too deadly.  Now their heads should face the player and the breath attack particles should shoot more directly at you.

There are also things I call "vents" that use a very similar attack when you get too close to them.  This has been modified to have a slightly larger range, but they shoot straight up now.  Previously, especially in caves, these things could kill you without ever showing you where they were.  

[h1]Star Database Improvements[/h1]
Navigating the Star Explorers galaxy has never been easier.  With the new update, you will be able to select a star in the database, and your ship will be pointing directly at it when you return to the view screen.  Also, if your overlay is active, the selected star will be highlighted, just as if you had clicked on it.  The star's data will also appear in your main computer screen, under the view screen.  This will make it a lot easier to return to a star you've already visited, and to be sure you are going to the right one.

notes.title: Minor Update 4.6B
notes.content: I just tweaked the Jet Pack slightly.  It was still possible, unlikely, but possible, to get stuck on terrain if you landed on the exact wrong spot while your jet pack was fully expended.  Now it will very slowly refill even when you are not on the ground, allowing for these unfortunate situations to be rendered harmless.

notes.title: Beta Updated to Version 4.6A
notes.content:
I was able to fix a few more issues and tweak some features in the process.

[h1]New Stuff[/h1]
[list]
[*]Landscape "Clumping" - those large rock formations you find on some planets will now form larger clumps and will not be so evenly distributed on planet surfaces.  I feel it makes things a bit more interesting visually.  This will only effect new planets, not planets that are being reloaded.
[*]Mothership Store has "consumables" - The mothership will now carry regular items in the first few slots.  This means you will always have a place to go for fuel, repair kits, ammo etc... 
[*]Mothership cash - the mothership will now have a somewhat randomized amount of money available.  
[*]"Fireflies" on some planets - just a simple particle effect for some worlds.
[*]Jet Pack - let's call it the Jet Pack 1.0.  Instead of jumping, your character now uses a small jet pack.  I never really liked the jump mechanic, which allowed you to jump based on the gravity of the planet.  The problem was that larger planets barely let you jump at all, which, though realistic, was kind of annoying.  The jet pack allows you to jump higher, but falling speed still depends on the gravity.  I may add fall damage, if I feel like it, but for now enjoy more freedom of movement.  This also became necessary because the new landscapes allowed you to get stuck, and I needed a way to escape from being wedged in between two rocks.
[/list]

[h1]Fixes[/h1]
[list]
[*]Ancient Artifact achievement should now be working - it will retroactively give you the achievement if you have constructed the hyperdive also.
[/list]

notes.title: Beta Updated to Version 4.6

[*]Lore has been added to the game for your reading enjoyment, but you will have to find it first!
[*]An overlay circle has been added to the mothership (while overlay "O" is active) when mothership is selected - previously only stars had this feature.
[/list]

[h1]Fixes[/h1]
[list]
[*]Certain roacks were floating on some planets.  This feature was fixed in the last version, but it lead to other objects disappearing.  All should be working now.
[*]Heat vents in caves should not be able to hurt the player unless they are in the appropriate range now.
[*]Orbit function has been tweaked and I hope it is more smooth now.  I believe i limited or removed the possibility of the ship turning the wrong way to reach a planet.  If you are "upside down" or oriented unusually, you may still experience this, as it also still happens with stars sometimes.  But it should be less often.
[*]Save option should now appear in menu after reaching mothership.  [*]Previously, it would not appear unless you left the console and returned to it.
[*]Spaceship movement should now continue after leaving console (while not in warp).  Warping always worked in this capacity, but if you were manually driving the ship, then stepped away from the console, the view screed would show the ship as not moving.  Once returning to the console, the ship would continue to move again.  Not a major issue, but I thought it should be consistent.
[/list]

notes.title: Beta Updated to Version 4.5A
notes.content:
The beta version has been updated once again.  It's a small update with big implications.

[h1]New Features[/h1]
Some new footsteps sounds have been added - you may notice that the sounds made will depend on what you are walking/running on.

[h1]Main Menu Button[/h1]
This was a big flaw in the UI design.  The game would cause errors if you tried to load a previously saved game after starting a game.  It also would not allow you to reload a game properly after crashing into a star.  Also, load was disabled if you died on a planet or in a cave.  

The solution is a bit of a hack, but it seems stable, and that's what most important.  I simply included a "Main Menu" button, which cleverly restarts the game, and allows you to reload your saved game or start a new one.  This circumvents a whole bunch of problems I faced while trying to load games while the game was active.  

[h1]Progress Warning[/h1]
There is a warning to let players know that their progress will be lost if they go back to the main menu, so make sure you save your game before you try to load another one.  

However, to prevent the ruination of otherwise good games, it will not allow you to save the game after your character has died.  

I think I've covered all the bases on this issue, but let me know if you experience any trouble with it.

notes.title: Final Release Underway
notes.content:
Well, this is it folks.  I am calling this game (almost) finished.  It will go to full release in May, and I will spend the remainder of my time in fixing any remaining bugs and refining some of the existing game elements.  

[h1]Report Bugs[/h1]
So if you have experienced anything strange, crashes, bugs or simply confusing aspects of gameplay, now is the time to let me know.  You can write it in the discussion forum, or shoot be an email, or a private message, or simply ignore this request, the choice is yours.  

[h1]The Manual[/h1]
Have a look at the manual I uploaded yesterday.  See if it makes sense or is missing anything important.  I do plan to add a section on inventory and upgrading your space suit.  Otherwise I think it covers all the bases.  

In the remaining improvements, I am including things like balancing item costs and availability.  In the beta version, I have made some subtle changes to what kinds of items appear at the mothership.  I have tweaked the costs of items and amounts of things like fuel crystals.

Achievements can be added.  Are there any things you'd like to see added to the achievements?  

[h1]New Features Suspended[/h1]
I don't think I will be overhauling the spaceship as I may have suggested.  Not at this time anyway.  In the future, if my 3D art skills improve, I may consider returning to this game and updating things, but for now the graphics are pretty much set.  

[h1]Inventory Bug[/h1]
I have reason to believe that the recent inventory bug I experienced was due to it being from an old saved game.  There was an issue when building items from blueprints, but that was resolved.  When testing the game, I loaded an old file, and noticed the same problem, forgetting that it was something I had fixed in the mean time.  However, if anyone experiences an inventory slot getting "disabled" please let me know about it.

notes.title: Beta Updated to 4.3
notes.content:
I have just updated the Beta to Version 4.3
Lots of new features and fixes this time around, here is a summary of the main ones:

[h1]Map Scanner[/h1][list]
[*]You now have a small top-down mapping device in the default weapon position (instead of nothing) so you can always see the closest way to the landing craft.  It also points to caves once you find them. 
[*]Caves you have entered are colored blue, so you'll know which ones you've been in already.
[*]It also works in caves, pointing the way back to the exit.
[/list]
[h1]Tutorial[/h1]
[list]
[*]Pressing TAB will open a context based tutorial for new players.  
[*]Depending on where you are in the game, it will remind you of your main objective, and give hints on what you can do in your current situation.
[/list]
[h1]Planet Update[/h1]
[list]
[*]Planets are now solid objects with their own gravity.  You can no longer pass through them, and you will crash if you are pulled in too close.  
[*]When leaving orbit, you will see a warning, and may have to hold down "S" until you are clear of the gravity well.
[*]The orbit graphic has also been updated to look more circular.
[/list]
[h1]Player Updates[/h1]
[list]
[*]Your weapon is now lowered and raised up whenever you switch weapons or reload.  It's just a visual effect that makes a little more sense, but I am too lazy ... er ... busy to do real reload animation at this point.
[*]Player oxygen will run out a little slower, and movement will not slow down as rapidly when damage is taken. 
[*]Only after reaching 50% or less will the player start slowing down.
[/list]
[h1]Effects[/h1]
[list]
[*]Weather Effects - rain, thunder, lightning, snow
[*]Lava Effects - lava steam and improved lava texture
[*]Lava planets are hotter now.  You will no longer freeze to death while submerged in lava :)
[*]Ice levels have also been updated with a new ice texture.  It's no longer a mirror, but the frame rate has been improved a lot.  
[*]Space dust is now darker and somewhat purple in color - it got a bit confusing to fins stars some times.
[/list]
[h1]Resolution Issue[/h1]
[list]
[*]This may be controversial but I have limited the screen resolution to a maximum width of 1280. 
[*]Fonts and certain effects were not scaling up or down to match the resolution, so the game looked off when using higher or lower screen widths.  
[*]To ensure a consistent experience, this is the best way to prevent strange errors like those mentioned in the short term.
[*]I am open to feedback on this, and I am considering how to resolve those issues while retaining higher resolution options. However, the game is not really cutting edge in terms of its visual appearence, so if this does not bother too many people I may keep it this way.  
[/list]
[h1]Other Fixes[/h1]
[list]
[*]Loading issues occurred if you wrote your name then cancelled in the new game menu.  Those should be resolved.
[*]Quest prices have been increased in some cases, and decreased in others.
[*]Ice should now reload correctly when returning to an ice planet
[*]Ores that are blasted from rocks should not get stuck in mid-air anymore.
[*]Floater should reload with a planet correctly (they were disappearing on revisiting some worlds)
[/list]
I was getting a game crash with the new mapping scanner, but I have resolved that issue, and all subsequent testing has resulted in no errors.  Let me know if this causes any issues for you.  

I am also narrowing down the cause of the terrain generation bug.  It seems to happen on worlds with a vapor atmosphere.  Avoid those worlds if you want to avoid this bug for now.  If you do encounter it, it will stop right when it looks like the terrain would be fully generated, just before adding features like rocks etc... when the loading bar is halfway across.  If it happens, please send me the file generated.

[*]This may be controversial but I have limited the screen resolution to a maximum width of 1280. 
[*]Fonts and certain effects were not scaling up or down to match the resolution, so the game looked off when using higher or lower screen widths.  
[*]To ensure a consistent experience, this is the best way to prevent strange errors like those mentioned in the short term.
[*]I am open to feedback on this, and I am considering how to resolve those issues while retaining higher resolution options. However, the game is not really cutting edge in terms of its visual appearence, so if this does not bother too many people I may keep it this way.  
[/list]
[h1]Other Fixes[/h1]
[list]
[*]Loading issues occurred if you wrote your name then cancelled in the new game menu.  Those should be resolved.
[*]Quest prices have been increased in some cases, and decreased in others.
[*]Ice should now reload correctly when returning to an ice planet
[*]Ores that are blasted from rocks should not get stuck in mid-air anymore.
[*]Floater should reload with a planet correctly (they were disappearing on revisiting some worlds)
[/list]
I was getting a game crash with the new mapping scanner, but I have resolved that issue, and all subsequent testing has resulted in no errors.  Let me know if this causes any issues for you.  

I am also narrowing down the cause of the terrain generation bug.  It seems to happen on worlds with a vapor atmosphere.  Avoid those worlds if you want to avoid this bug for now.  If you do encounter it, it will stop right when it looks like the terrain would be fully generated, just before adding features like rocks etc... when the loading bar is halfway across.  If it happens, please send me the file generated.

notes.title: Feedback Requested
notes.content:
[h1]Balance[/h1]
I am trying to spend time on streamlining and balancing the game now.  New features like blueprints have been tested as to whether they work or not, but how aboout how they feel?  Are too many items required to build something?  Too few?  

Is it too hard to get certain items, or too easy to get others?  

Do you find yourself with too much money and nothing to spend it on?  Or are you too poor to afford even basic equipment?  

Star Explorers is not meant to be easy, but it is not meant to fell impossible either.  Finding the right balance in a procedural game can be difficult, but with your feedback, it will be easier for me to get things as close to balanced as possible. 

[h1]Instructions[/h1]
Star Explorers is somewhat complex, especially for new players.  I want to include a game manual, but I'm wondering if this will be enough.  Do players need interactive in-game tutorials these days?  I personally prefer a manual that I can refer to, but I am an old game player.  Currently, the ship's computer has a very basic tutorial on what you can do in each phase of the game, but it does not shout out at the player.  

I think a pdf manual, included with the game, and a video tutorial here on Steam should be enough to get people started.  What do you think?

[h1]Polish[/h1]
Polish, not Polish ... anyway, I realize that Star Explorers has a 90's game look and feel, and this is pretty much where it's going to stay.  As a solo developer there is only so much I can do before exhaustion sets in.  I definitely plan to update the mothership model, though, that is clearly an unfinished, but important visual aspect of the game.  

My question to you is whether there is any other part of the game that seems too rough or unfinished to release?  If you say "all of it" point taken, but I am looking for constructive feedback.  

[h1]Release[/h1]
I do plan to fully release Star Explorers by the end of May 2018.  Overall it seems to be running more stable than ever (God I hope this is really true) and I definitely need to step back from it for a while.  I don't expect a huge commercial success, and I plan to cut down on the scope of my future projects a lot.  

Ultimately, I feel like I did accomplish what I set out to do, Star Explorers has all the features I put in my original design document, but with quite a few big studios doing very similar games, I do not expect it to change the gaming world in any way at this point.  For everyone who purchased the game, and provided critical feedback, I thank you.  

[h1]Star Explorers - The Album[/h1]
As a free gift for anyone, I offer you the Star Explorers Soundrack:
https://mkschmidt.bandcamp.com/album/star-explorers

This is a collection of songs generated by the game's music algorithm.  Every play-through, planet and cave will produce different music on the fly when you play Star Explorers.  These were all songs that stood out for me while testing the game.  

[h1]Star Explorers - Music Generator[/h1]
Also, if you are a game developer or musician, I also give you the right to use any music generated by Star Explorers (or for that matter, my other game Anomalies, which uses a very different music algorithm) at no additional cost.  I would appreciate a reference to the game if you do end up recording and using any of the music though, that would be nice! 

For recording, you can use Audacity or any other audio recording software.  Make sure you turn down the main volume, and turn up the music before recording.

notes.title: Beta Version 4.0 now Active
notes.content:
If you are running the beta version of Star Explorers, you should be getting an update.  The new version 4.0 is a brand new build of the game that will require players to start a new game.  If you do not want to start a new game, keep using the default version (which is the same build as the previous beta).  

[h1]IMPORTANT[/h1]
If you do choose to start a new game, take the extra time to uninstall Star Explorers completely, then reinstall it.  There are problems that occurred with the last build which may have been caused by some descrepancy betwen the various builds of the game.  In order to eliminate this as a possibility, a fresh install will rule that out.

The new version has a number of improvements and new features, here's a list of what to expect.  The new features list is rather short but offers some significant gameplay changes.

[h1]New Features[/h1]
[list]
[*]New Unique Blueprint Items - you'll have to find them to see what they are.
[*]Locked Doors - some special places now require a key to get into.
[*]Solar/Manual Engine Limit - Solar and manual engines are now limited to working only in the current solar system or near the mothership.  
[/list]

[h1]Fixes[/h1]
[list]
[*]Updated Terrain Generator - this time the terrain generator tests for terrain errors while building.  Terrains larger than the default 14 x 14 (set in Video Options) may reduce your framerate, will take a longer time to generate, and will be more likely to cause the types of errors seen in previous builds.  So far it seems to be working even on large terrains, but if you are feeling adventurous, try it out.
[*]Errent Sectors - there was a bug that allowed sectors to show up in the star chart that do not actually exist in the game.  This should no longer occur.
[*]Landscape Flash - on planets, terrain objects would occasionally disappear and pop back into existence.  Transitions should now be smoother, however it may reduce the framerate on slower machines.  If the framerate reduction is significant, let me know. 
[*]Storage Info Crash - Occasionally, reloading a planet would get stuck on "Updating Storage Info." This has been resolved, and should no longer occur.
[*]Ice Model Updated - Well, it looks exactly the same, but I reduced the number of polygons on the mirror ice model.  This should improve the framerate on ice planets slightly.
[/list]

My plan is to keep working on this version until the full release in May.  I do not plan to add any new features that will require starting a new game.  My focus will be on resolvine any remaining bugs, and streamlining the gameplay.  

As always, let me know if you encounter any problems with the update, should you decide to use it.

notes.title: Star Explorers Default Game Updated
notes.content:
The Default Star Explorers game has been updated to Beta Version 3.4D.

Before I describe all the new features and benefits of 3.4D, let me address those of you who are currently playing the default version.  Your saved game will not load in the new version.  However, if you want to continue your existing game, you can opt to use the "legacy" version by right clicking on Star Explorers>Properties>Betas>legacy.  This will reload the old version of the game and allow you to continue where you left off.

You may also need to delete your existing "settings.cfg" file in order for it to work correctly.  Check Star Explorers>Properties>Local Files>Browse Local Files and delete "Settings.cfg" before you start a new game.

For those of you who want to go with the update, know that the game is still in Early Access, and it is still incomplete, however a number of improvements have been made and new features have been added.

To see details about all of these, please see all the previous announcements.  In short, they are as follows:

[h1]New Features[/h1]
[list]
[*]New Terrain Generator
[*]Blueprint based crafting system
[*]Storage locker on ship
[*]Improved alien A.I. and collision functions
[*]Updated loading bar with a text description of what is happening
[*]More stable code for menus and other aspects of the game, many potential crashes have been fixed.
[/list]

[h1]About Early Access[/h1]
As many people pointed out early on, the game was not quite complete and polished enough for an early access release.  I accept this criticism.  If I could do it over, I would probably have waited a bit longer and polished the game up a bit more before releasing.  On the other hand, it has been the contributions of players in Early Access that have allowed me to find and make improvements to the game.  For me that is how I understood Early Access, and it is basically working out that way.  [url=http://store.steampowered.com/earlyaccessfaq/]Steam's guidelines[/url] on this are pretty vague.  However from a marketing standpoint, I accept that releasing a game too early can have a negative impact on players.  

[img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/28731582/2c283b8054ea2f88962b311b5c572f11a83faa64.jpg[/img]

With that said, If you purchased Star Explorers, it is very helpful to me if you play the game and offer your criticism.  Preferrably in the discussion board if possible.   

Thanks again for your continued interest in Star Explorers!

notes.title: Version 3.4D Solves Materials Issue with Blueprints
notes.content:
The latest update 3.4D under Properties>Betas>Beta finally solves the issue we were seeing where the second material in a blueprint would get set to zero.  

I was looking in more recent scripts, since it appeared to be a new problem, however, it turns out that this issues has been active since Star Explorers was released in May of last year.  

The reason it turned up now is that very few items actually use all the data slots like blueprints do.  Only weapons and space suits would have been effected by this problem, and it makes sense that when a player finds a new weapon or suit, they would want to equip it as soon as possible.  

The issue would only have effected items that were stored in the second row of the player's backpack, and then only when the player picked up items like crystals or ores, and they were alloted to the third (last) row of the backpack.  Essentially data of these items was being written to the wrong slot, and it would set some of the items in the previous row's statistics to zero or otherwise incorrect values.  

3.4D fixes this once and for all.  However, any blueprints or other items that were already corrupted in this way will remain corrupted.  

Now I can go back to expanding the game.  Let me know if you have any questions or find any other bugs!

notes.title: Beta Version 3.4A
notes.content:
I have updated the Beta Version to 3.4A.  Why the letter, and not 3.5?  Well, there is no actual new content, just a couple fixes for things that were not working correctly.

[h1]What's Fixed?[/h1]
[list]
[*]Storage Locker on ship now seems to retain all its contents between saves/loads
[*]Storage caches on planets - I found a potential cause for their disappearances, so they should remain persistent now
[*]Terrain Glitches - I have a version of the game in which I am refining and improving the terrain generator, but for now I have limited the max terrain size to 14, which seems fairly stable
[*]Blueprint materials - now when you use up a material it will properly remove it from your inventory, instead of just setting its quantity to zero
[*]I fixed a major problem where planet files were written incorrectly, and would not reload.  The loading bar would go up, but the little number would be stuck at 992 and it would say "regenerating terrain features".  I'm not sure if this issue existed in the previous version, or if it was something I introduced while "fixing" the terrain generator, but hopefully it will not cause any more trouble.
[/list]

As always, thanks for all your help in play-testing this early access game.  With a procedural galaxy like the one in Star Explorers, it's virtually impossible for me to test all the different combinations and potential outcomes.  Having kind people like you (this means you) play-testing the game, makes it possible for me to continue working on it consistently.

notes.title: Beta Version 3.4
notes.content:
I have updated the Beta to Version 3.4.  

[h1]Terrain Update[/h1]
After my terrain stress-testing, I am almost completely, pretty darn, mostly confident that we will not see any more terrain discrepancies.  I found 3 potential causes for the problems, and have either fixed them directly, or in one case, forced the terrain to restart when encountered.  In any case, it should be considerably more stable than the previous version.  

[h1]The Escape Clause[/h1]
Also addressed is the escape key issue.  A kind player had pointed out that the escape key was causing the game to exit prematurely.  This was only happening before you started a new game, or loaded a previously saved game, but it has been fixed.  Currently, the escape key does not do anything until after you load a game.  I may add the functionality to exit open menus, as it does once your game is loaded.  

[h1]Storage Cache[/h1]
The storage cache on your spaceship should be more stable now.  I found a potential cause for its missing items.  I did notice that one slot was not working properly, so there may be some issues remaining with this feature.  The items were properly placed, and could be removed successfully, but the item's image would not be seen in one slot (third slot in the top row).  I will be investigating this problem further.

[h1]New Bug![/h1]
I also noticed a new bug.  If you load or start a game, then load another game while on the spaceship, it will load, but the game may not function correctly.  I normally don't do this, I would only load a game at the beginning, or after dying of suffocation or some other hazard on a planet, so this type of loading was not properly tested.  For now, if you need to load a saved game, it's best to restart Star Explorers.

This was only happening before you started a new game, or loaded a previously saved game, but it has been fixed.  Currently, the escape key does not do anything until after you load a game.  I may add the functionality to exit open menus, as it does once your game is loaded.  

[h1]Storage Cache[/h1]
The storage cache on your spaceship should be more stable now.  I found a potential cause for its missing items.  I did notice that one slot was not working properly, so there may be some issues remaining with this feature.  The items were properly placed, and could be removed successfully, but the item's image would not be seen in one slot (third slot in the top row).  I will be investigating this problem further.

[h1]New Bug![/h1]
I also noticed a new bug.  If you load or start a game, then load another game while on the spaceship, it will load, but the game may not function correctly.  I normally don't do this, I would only load a game at the beginning, or after dying of suffocation or some other hazard on a planet, so this type of loading was not properly tested.  For now, if you need to load a saved game, it's best to restart Star Explorers.

notes.title: Beta Version 3.3 Update
notes.content:
A few improvements have been made

[h1]Ship Storage Cache[/h1]
Your spaceship now has a storage locker.  You know that hallway that leads to a solid door that does nothing?  Well, now it is a storage cache, where you can keep surpluss items.  This became really necessary once all the new materials and blueprints were added.  

[img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/28731582/87919bc824ce8f2dffddd67eea31ddf007cab752.jpg[/img]

[h1]Fixed Planet Storage[/h1]

notes.title: Beta Version 3.2 (Update Jan 22nd 2018)
notes.content:
Star Explorers beta has been updated to version 3.2.  To access the beta, go to Star Explorers>Properties>Betas and choose Beta from the drop down.  It should automatically download the updated version.

Note: The "Testing" version is for me to use, prior to updating the Beta.  Sometimes I upload the game, but a file is missing or some other error occurrs, so I like to run it online before pushing the new version into the Beta Slot.

The Beta version is the latest, tested version of the game, but since my ability to test is limited, I like to get feedback from some players before I push it to the defautl version.  

Also Note: If you are planning to continue playing a game you started in the default version, do not update to the Beta version yet.  The beta will not open games that were started in the default (older) version of Star Explorers.  I try to avoid this as much as possible, but some updates are to big and complex to allow for earlier saved games to work.  

[h1]Blueprints[/h1]
[list]
[*]Blueprints have been added to the 3.2 Beta.
[*]Blueprints allow you to build items with materials you find throughout the game.
[*]A number of materials have been added to the game, so look for them in caves and in treasure chests, and buy them from alien traders or the mothership. 
[*]Blueprints are working, but I have plans to add new items that you will only be able to get by building them with a blueprint
[/list]

[h1]Cave Obstructions[/h1]
[list]
[*]Some caves and ancient ruins might have a group of rocks or wall that is blocking you from exploring too far.  
[*]This is not an error.  
[*]Find a way around, or a means of breaking through these barriers. 
[*]I will leave it to players to figure out how to do this.  
[/list]

[h1]Fixed Database[/h1]
[list]
[*]There was a problem with the galactic database.
[*]Star names would appear in the detail panel based on the sector location of the spaceship, rather than the sector selected in the star chart.
[*]Any stars renamed, or notes added, would get assigned to the wrong star, if they were edited in a sector other than the one they are in.
[*]This should be functioning correctly now.
[/list]

[h1]Other Fixes[/h1]
[list]
[*]When exiting ruins, player should not get stuck under the stairway anymore.
[*]Aliens that are somewhat smaller should bahave in a rational manner now.  I had to extend their attack range slightly, because they were unable to hit the player, and would continue to crawl underneath him, causing all sorts of problems.
[*]Cache boxes in caves should now rest at the correct height.
[/list]

Once I complete my plans for the blueprints, introducing unique items that the player can build, I will begin a more intense testing round, and push the Beta up to the default version.  The old version might be kept on as a legacy version of the game, so anyone who started a game may opt to complete it.

notes.title: Update January 12th 2018
notes.content:
[h1]Perpetual Worlds are Here![/h1]
The new Beta Version 3.1 includes a few new features, most important of which is it's ability to save data in planet and cave loot boxes, and bipedal aliens.  

Now, if you put something in a loot box, and leave that planet or cave, you will find the same items there the next time you return.  Also, if a certain alien is offering something for sale, or has a particular quest, you may now leave the planet in order to collect money, or find the quest item, then return and make the transaction.  

Of course, this is how Star Explorers was intended to work from the beginning, I just hadn't come up with a good way to do it until now.  Note: This feature will only work on chests that were created in the new version (3.1) of the game.  Chests that were created in the older version (3.0) will still load when you return to a previously saved planet or cave, but they will not have the same items in them from before the update.  However, if you return to the the same cave or planet again, later, any items should be there.  This is because the new script creates a new save file whenever you leave a planet or cave.  If the save file is not there, but you are reloading an old planet, it will work the old way, and repopulate the cache with items (or not).  Once you leave that location, any items will be then written into the new save file, and they will be persistent on any subsequent visits.

[h1]WARNING![/h1]
If you are attempting the Beta 3.1 version (or the previous 3.0 for that matter) you may encounter a crash when trying to land on a planet.  This can be resolved by making sure you set the Video Options before playing the game.  If the game reads your old settings file, a crucial variable will be missing, and the game will not load planets correctly.  Setting the video options and clicking Okay, will reset this variable, and allow planets to load normally.  This only needs to be done once.  

Another way to do it would be to navigate to your Properties>Local Files>Browse Local Files, and delete the "settings.cfg" file before playing the new Beta version.  

This should not effect any new installations of Star Explorers, only for those who had installed the game before the Beta 3.0 update.

[h1]Other Features[/h1]
[list]
[*]I fixed a number of minor bugs, most of which were caused by the new perpetual world script.  
[*]Item Scan - Certain things like grass models, and cave walls would interfere with the item_scan function, which allows you to pick up items or open caches.  This should be resolved, and getting that little hand icon (indicating that you can interact) to show up should be easier now.  
[*]Floater Types - those weird little floating aliens actually have a number of different possible forms.  Some of these forms were mistakenly disabled since they were added to the game, and I only just caught this issue.  If you explore enough, you may encounter some different types of floaters (some of which do not actually float at all)
[*]Shadows - There was a problem where if you turned shadows off, then tried to turn them on again, they would not appear.  This should now be resolved.  However, if you encounter this problem, the easiest way to fix it would be to delete your "settings.cfg" file.  If you want you could also edit it so that the number after "shadow alpha" is set to 75 instead of 0.  This would only effect someone who turned off Real-Time-Shadows in the Video Options menu in the Beta 3.0 release.
[*]Invalid arguments in Cave_Load - I encountered this issue, and I beleive it should be gone now.  However, I am a bit concerned at how water and ice shaders might be effected.  If you notice any problems with the reflective ice, or water effects, especially after leaving a cave, please let me know.

notes.title: Another update to the Beta
notes.content:
Beta Version 3.0 (accessible via Star Explorers>Properties>Betas>Beta) has received another update.  This time the following things have been fixed:

[h1]Game Save Issue[/h1]
[list]
[*]Previously, if you started a new game, then exited prior to saving at a star system, the game would load correctly, but planets would not properly orbit their stars anymore.
[*]Now you should be able to save the game at any location in the galaxy - as long as you are at the helm of your spaceship, and reload the game with no problems.  
[*]This means you may save at the mothership - which I had always intended for the game to allow.
[*]Note: You still cannot save during a warp or planet approach, but you can save while in orbit of a planet.
[/list]


[h1]Terrain Glitch[/h1]
[list]
[*]The game creates an endless planet surface by making a fake terrain just outside of the real terrain, so the player will not realise he is actually teleporting from one side of the map to another.
[*]This system was flawed, since you could see a glitch each time you teleported from one side of the terrain to another.
[*]I found a curious piece of code that was causing the grass to try and reposition itself manually, by tracing a new surface position each time this happened.  This led to a massive framerate drop, but only for one frame, after which the game would run normally again.
[*]I fixed the code, so that the grass would not have to reposition itself manually, but simply jumps to the new position.
[*]This new approach makes the jump effect virtually seamless, and there is no framerate drop when passing over the edges of the map.
[*]If you can't tell, I'm very happy about this discovery :)
[*]I believe it also solved the problem of grass jumping to different positions with each of these transitions, but I was unable to actually reproduce that problem, so it may show up again.
[/list]

[h1]Jumping[/h1]
[list]
[*]Jumping has been normalized for all gravity levels.  Low gravity planets were allowing the player to jump a bit too high, and high gravity planets were not allowing jumping at all in some cases.
[*]Player was getting stuck in cave ceilings - this has been fixed
[*]Player was jumping immedietly on loading a new planet or cave, now player should start at ground level
[/list]

[h1]Other Stuff[/h1]
[list]
[*]Crates/Caches now make the proper closing sound again.
[*]Some rocks and Speleotherms (Stalagmites and Stalagtites) are now destructable with the rocket launcher - this will be used to create some more interesting experiences, like clearing blocked passages or perhaps releasing hidden items like crystals or ores.
[/list]
