notes.title: Major Stability Update - Beta Version 3.0 Now Available for Testing
notes.content:
I have just made the Beta 3.0 version of Star Explorers available for testing.  This is a significant update, and unfortunately will not load previously saved games.  Here's what's fixed and what's new:

[h1]Planet Updates[/h1]
[list]
[*]A new terrain generator may not look too different, but it is more stable and allows for bigger planets
[*]Player and NPC collision - New collision functions prevent player and NPCs from going through landscape features
[*]Updated A.I. Along with collision detection, aliens do do not "shake" back and forth when approaching or running away from the player
[*]Bipedal aliens will now jump from time to time
[*]Bipedal aliens now carry visible weapons, and will drop them if defeated
[*]Bipedal aliens laser sound volume is now controlled with the volume slider, like everything else
[*]Clip distance has been optimized to improve performance
[*]Updated script that controls terrain features allows features to "jump" from one part of the planet to another - this reduces the total number of objects on each planet significantly - the previous script created copies of each object - it should also improve performance
[*]Previous version sometimes encountered an "invalid arguments" error when leaving planets - this should no longer happen
[/list]

[h1]Player & Controls[/h1]
[list]
[*]Player will gain health slowly when aboard the spaceship
[*]Updated script prevents controls from "sticking" 
[*]Updated flashlight - shines more consistently on grass features
[*]Money is now handled fully as integers - there were some items that allowed decimal places in the value, causing some confusion when buying and selling
[/list]

[h1]New Video Options[/h1]
[list]
[*]Shadows - turn shadow effects on or off to improve performance
[*]Bloom - turn bloom feature on or off as preferred, and for possible performance boost (when off)
[*]Max Planet Size - large planets may run slower on some machines- if you experience problems, you can reduce the maximum size planets will form - you may also choose to increase the size above the default max size of 14 (planets are created on a grid, in this case 14 x 14 tiles)
[*]Terrain Density - grass, rocks, trees, plants and more are effected by this number - lowering this slider will make your planets look a little barren, but will improve performance
[/list]


[h1]Other Fixes[/h1]
[list]
[*]Warping to a nearby star (especially after completing a mission, when the mothership moves near) was causing a problem, and getting the spaceshp stuck in warp - this should no longer be an issue.
[*]Oxygen planets will now replenish your oxygen tank when above the surface of any liquid body  
[*]Incomplete Fungi - the previous version allowed fungi to appear incomplete and/or floating in the air - this should no longer happen
[*]Cave laser issue - previous builds would prevent the player from firing in caves when facing a certain direction - this should be working now
[*]Problem in database caused a problem when trying to rename stars - this should work fine now
[*]Another problem would prevent player from writing longer names, or additional notes in a star's entry (I just realised I need to fix this in the planet database too)
[/list]

[h1]Notes[/h1]
To access the Beta 3.0 version, go to Star Explorers > Properties > Betas and select "beta" from the drop down.  

You will need to start a new game to test it.

I will keep the "default" and "testing" versions active for anyone who wants to complete an existing game.  Once the new version is made to "default" I will create a "legacy" version for old players who still want to complete an older game.  

This update was more about stability and consistency, not many new features are present.  

There are a couple known issues that are either things I had not noticed before, or they were introduced as a result of these changes. 

[h1]Known Issues[/h1]
[list]
[*]Grass jumping - when the player crosses over the "edge" of a planet, terrain features "jump" to make it appear that he has gone around the whole planet - when this happens, sometimes the grass or small rocks seem to jump into different positions - I'm working on fixing it
[*]The new collision features have caused the player to jump somewhat differently - it seems to work fine on planet surfaces, but there are some strange results in caves - jumping is not a major part of the gameplay at this point so I allowed this to pass for now
[*]Save game in a star system - if you start a new game, then exit before saving near a star system (after warping to it) the game will not load correctly, and you will have to start a new one - this is the next big issue I will be fixing
[/list]

[h1]Final Important Statement[/h1]
When testing the game I use the default video settings - 1280 x 720 and in windowed mode, also keeping planet sizes limited to 14 and density limited to .5.  I have tested full screen, and changing the window size, but I am referring to playing through the whole game.  There may be issues that pop up in different video modes that I have not encountered.  For best performance, keep the video setting on default.  

If anyone prefers changing the screen size or going in full screen mode, feel free to do so.  Please let me know if you encounter any errors.

This last request applies to everyone.  There are so many different combinations of features and events that can occur in a generatively designed game like Star Explorers.  It's impossible to test every possible combination of actions and events.  If you do encounter errors, I would love to know about them.  Finishing the game, and making it as stable as possible for its full release (still planned for May of 2018) is my top priority

And Happy New Year!

I will keep the "default" and "testing" versions active for anyone who wants to complete an existing game.  Once the new version is made to "default" I will create a "legacy" version for old players who still want to complete an older game.  

This update was more about stability and consistency, not many new features are present.  

There are a couple known issues that are either things I had not noticed before, or they were introduced as a result of these changes. 

[h1]Known Issues[/h1]
[list]
[*]Grass jumping - when the player crosses over the "edge" of a planet, terrain features "jump" to make it appear that he has gone around the whole planet - when this happens, sometimes the grass or small rocks seem to jump into different positions - I'm working on fixing it
[*]The new collision features have caused the player to jump somewhat differently - it seems to work fine on planet surfaces, but there are some strange results in caves - jumping is not a major part of the gameplay at this point so I allowed this to pass for now
[*]Save game in a star system - if you start a new game, then exit before saving near a star system (after warping to it) the game will not load correctly, and you will have to start a new one - this is the next big issue I will be fixing
[/list]

[h1]Final Important Statement[/h1]
When testing the game I use the default video settings - 1280 x 720 and in windowed mode, also keeping planet sizes limited to 14 and density limited to .5.  I have tested full screen, and changing the window size, but I am referring to playing through the whole game.  There may be issues that pop up in different video modes that I have not encountered.  For best performance, keep the video setting on default.  

If anyone prefers changing the screen size or going in full screen mode, feel free to do so.  Please let me know if you encounter any errors.

This last request applies to everyone.  There are so many different combinations of features and events that can occur in a generatively designed game like Star Explorers.  It's impossible to test every possible combination of actions and events.  If you do encounter errors, I would love to know about them.  Finishing the game, and making it as stable as possible for its full release (still planned for May of 2018) is my top priority

And Happy New Year!

notes.title: Terrain Generation Update
notes.content:
Right now, I'm working on updating the terrain generation script.  It works okay in the current game build, but if I increase the planet size, it tends to generate errors with the placement of tiles quite often.  

I have re-written the script from scratch, in order to weed out these errors, and so far it appears to be much more stable.  Current planet surfaces are 12 x 12 tiles, but I have successfully created terrains more than 24 x 24 tiles with the new script.  I don't know if they will get that big in-game, as there are other factors, like frame-rate, that will dictate the limits.  

Here is a short video of the new script in action

http://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=1237507849

I think I will give players the option to dictate planet size limits, kind of like Minecraft, so they can optimize the game to work best on their own systems.  

I have incorporated this new script into the game, and I am working on getting it to work with all the other features, like placement of rocks, plants, caves, etc...  It should be ready in the next few days.

notes.title: Update December 8th 2017
notes.content:
The following new features and fixes have been implemented in the "Testing" version.

[h1]Landing Craft[/h1]
[list]
[*]The landing craft will no longer give health or repair your suit, but it will fill up your oxygen.
[*]This was always supposed to be a temporary feature.  It is being replaced by Kits, described below.
[/list]

[h1]Kits[/h1]
[list]
[*]Three new items have been added to the game. 
[*]Health Kit: Allows you to revive your health when you are injured.    
[*]Repair Kit: Allows you to repair your space suit when it is damaged.
[*]Oxygen Tank: Allows you to replenish your oxygen when it is low.
[*]Kits are available at the mothership and can be found in caches throughout the game.  They are "Stackable" like crystals, so they should not take up too much room in your inventory.
[/list]

[h1]Menu Overhaul[/h1]
[list]
[*]In an effort to streamline Star Explorers, I have overhauled the menu system. 
[*]Before you get too excited, it appears identical to the previous menu system.    
[*]I spent a lot of time revising my code, taking out redundancies and making sure all the different kinds of menus, panels and viewports interact smoothly.
[*]Previously, the mouse cursor would freeze in certain circumstances.
[*]Previously, an equipped weapon would fire when closing a menu with the mouse button - this should not happen any more.
[*]There were a number of other minor problems and inneficient methods at play.  The whole system makes more sense now ... you would only know it by looking at the code though.
[/list]

notes.title: Update December 5th 2017
notes.content:
First and foremost, the crash after reloading a game has been fixed in the "Testing" version of Star Explorers.  Also, the following new features and fixes have been implemented, also in the "Testing" version.

[h1]Star Approach[/h1]
[list]
[*]When approaching a star, the game used to slow down considerably on the final approach.  This has been remedied, though there will still be a framerate drop for one moment during the trip. 
[*]A warp tunnel effect has been added - to look cool, but also to hide the more abrupt appearance of stars and planets.  
[*]The spaceship will now arrive at the edge of a solar system, rather than right next to it's star.
[/list]

[h1]Planet Lighting[/h1]
[list]
[*]The sky color for oxygen planets was somehow red before.  I have updated it to be blue.
[*]Planets should be brighter in general now.
[*]I plan to continue to tweak the planet colors and brightness, though it may not update already saved planets.  But it is nothing that will prevent anyone from playing saved games.
[/list]

[h1]Tab and F11[/h1]
[list]
[*]I have disabled these buttons, they were part of the engine debugging script, that should not be in a released game.  
[/list]

If you experience any trouble with these new features, please let me know about it.  Deleting your settings.cfg file will reset your game to default settings in case there is a conflict there.

notes.title: Update December 4th 2017
notes.content:
A few new features and tweaks have been added.  These should not interfere with currently saved games. These changes are currently only in the "Testing" version of Star Explorers.

[h1]Fullscreen Issue[/h1]
[list]
[*]The Fullscreen option has been changed slightly, to make it (hopefully) more user friendly.  Now, if you go to Options>Video, and you click on Fullscreen, then Okay, it will change the game to fullscreen matching your monitor's current screen resolution. 
[*]It used to attempt to go to fullscreen using the game screen resolution (which is 1280 x 720 by default) and this seems to have cause problems for some users, if their monitor did not support that resolution.  
[*]Hopefully this will solve any problems users have faced with screen resolution, but let me know if you encounter any other issues.
[/list]

[h1]Planet Sunlight[/h1]
[list]
[*]Suns seen from planet surfaces no longer appear to be moving fireballs when the player moves.
[*]Suns are also given a unique size, based on the star's actual size, and distance from the planet.
[*]Surface lighting is still based on the star's brightness and the planet's distance from its star, but the range has been limited for aesthetic reasons
[/list]

[h1]Orbit Jitter[/h1]
[list]
[*]There was a noticable jitter when your spaceship orbited a planet, especially when in full screen mode.  
[*]I believe I have fixed this issue, and orbit animation should now appear smooth at any screen resolution or mode.
[/list]

If you experience any trouble with these new features, please let me know about it.  Deleting your settings.cfg file will reset your game to default settings in case there is a conflict there.

notes.title: Update December 1st 2017
notes.content:
New features have been added to the "Testing" version of Star Explorers.  These should all integrate smoothly with existing saved games.  Let me know if you experience any trouble.  If you are unfamiliar with the "Testing" version of Star Explorers, scroll to the bottom to see how to activate it.

[h1]Key Binding[/h1]
[list]
[*]Under Options>Controls, you can now assign custom keys to player and ship actions.
[*]Rebound keys should be stored and reloaded between game sessions, so you should only need to customize keys once.  
[*]Note: Some actions are linked, like movement, opening inventory, etc... so there is no way to assign a different key to moving the ship forward vs. moving the player forward.  
[*]Note: The game will allow you to assign the same key to two different actions, but this will cause the previously assigned action to stop working.  For example, if you assign "F" to inventory, it will allow you to open your inventory, but it will no longer turn on your flashlight.  Make sure you assign unique keys to each action (aside from the aformentioned linked actions)
[*]If you encounter a problem assigning keys, there is a "reset" button on the lower left side of the controls menu. Use it to return all controls to default.
[/list]

[h1]New Computer Voice[/h1]
[list]
[*]A helpful female voice actor has provided the ship's computer with a pleasant new voice.
[*]This means that I am no longer the sole contributer to this game. 
[/list]

[h1]Other Fixes and Updates[/h1]
[list]
[*]The bloom shader has been tweaked to be much more subtle than before.
[*]Scanning objects has been tweaked, and should now be easier to use.  Scanning refers to when the small hand icon shows up, allowing you to interact with/pick up a game object.   
[/list]


[h1]Activating the "Testing" Version of Star Explorers[/h1]
In order to activate the "Testing" version of Star Explorers, take the following steps:
[list]
[*]Right click on Star Explorers in your game library.
[*]Select Properties
[*]Select the Betas tab
[*]Select "Testing" from the drop down menu
[/list]

This should put the game in the update queu, and allow you to explore these new, experimental features.  Once several other updates have accumulated, and they have proven themselves error free, I will be creating a new beta version of the game, which will be assigned as the default.  This will happen some time during December, before 2018 comes around.

notes.title: UPDATE: "Through the Time Vortex" Stretch Goal
notes.content:
I have added a stretch goal for the Star Explorers Indiegogo campaign called "Through the Time Vortex."  Since Open Galaxy Exploration games are now fairly common, I've decided to add a brand new game mechanic that allows the player to explore the past, present and future of each star system.  

This feature will only be added if the $25,000 stretch goal is reached.  Also, this feature will only be worked on after Star Explorers (in its current form) is completed and fully released on Steam.  "Through the Time Vortex" will be added as an optional DLC package once it is finished.  If these goals are met, I anticipate a release date of January 2018 for Star Explorers, and October 2018 for Through the Time Vortex.

Stay tuned for an updated video demonstrating this revolutionary game mechanic, and look out for some new perks (coming soon) to help facilitate this concept!  See the Indiegogo page under updates for more details: https://www.indiegogo.com/projects/star-explorers-space/x/17324659#/

notes.title: Screen Resolution - How to Set
notes.content:
My advice for changing screen resolutuion settings (in it's current state) is this:
1. Check your monitors resolution options. Take note of the size you want to use, and also a smaller size option.
2. Set your monitor to the largest size you want to use i.e. 1600 x 900.
3. In Star Explorers change the resolution in windowed mode to that smaller size option, i.e. 1360 x 768 and hit "Apply" (Don't go full screen yet) Your window should be 1360 x 768, on a 1600 x 900 monitor now.
4. Now return to the video options and select "Fullscreen" and hit apply.
5. Now your game should be full screen at 1360 x 768
6. Now you can reset the resolution to your preferred size (1600 x 900) and hit apply. It should retain it's full-screen status

It's not really user friendly, but it seems to work.  I plan on streamlining this and the rest of the UI and gameplay.

notes.title: Update Beta Version 2.2
notes.content:
I have updated both the testing and the default to Version 2.2.  This includes a new graphic feature, which is described below.  However, that main reason for the update is to eliminate a game crashing bug involving saving the game near the mothership.

[h1]Fixes[/h1]
[list]
[*]Removes the possibility of saving the game near the mothership.  Previously, saving near the mothership would cause the game to reload incorrectly.  You are now only able to save the game when near a star - this is a temporary fix until the underlying cause is rooted out.  
[*]Flashlight and Reload commands added to the controls menu (F and R)
[/list]


[h1]New Feature[/h1]
[list]
[*]Bloom Shader - you may notice this atmospheric effect on lights, stars, backgrounds and other bright surfaces.  
[/list]

As with other updates, feedback is always welcome.  If I have overlooked something that causes problems, please let me know.

notes.title: Update 08/24/2017
notes.content:
Once again the "Testing" version of Star Explorers has been updated.  It includes the following:

[list]
[*]New Warning Message - when entering a star's gravity well, a warning message will flash on and off when you are flying the spaceship
[*]New Alarm - in addition to the flashing message, and alarm will sound.  Both will remain on until you are able to exit the star's gravity well, or your ship crashes into the star.
[*]Selecting Planets and Stars - you can no longer select planets or stars that appear behind a star you are close to.  This should prevent the spaceship from crashing into a star while warping or attempting to orbit a planet.  Note, it can still crash if the planet is moving behind the star during the approach - I am working on a way to prevent this.
[*]Crashing while Warping - if you do choose to warp to a star, by selecting the warp option in the star chart, and if that star happens to be behind a nearby star, you will no longer crash into it.  Warping creates a pocket outside of space time, so you should not have to worry about crashing into physical objects while warping.  
[/list]

I will do some more testing tomorrow.  If I do not encounter any errors, I plan to update the changes to the default version of Star Explorers.

[*]New Leaf Types - There are five new leaf types, in addition to the original 5.  The new ones are much bigger, making trees a more prominent feature of some planets.  
[*]Leaf and Plant Shadows - Tree leaves and plants now cast shadows.

[img]http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/28731582/304861180585c1ae43ad7c9f04555c6ba61d72ba.jpg[/img]

notes.title: Update 07/25/2017
notes.content:
I have fixed a number of small bugs.  I will be unable to do much over the next couple weeks, so this will be the last update for a while.  However, I have some big plans that should get finished by the end of August.  For now, the following issues have been addressed:

This is my first attempt to balance out the monetary system in Star Explorers.  I noticed that geting crystals gave the player a lot of surpluss money, with very little to spend it on.  Having better, but more expensive armor upgrades will give the player something to do with that money, and each upgrade will allow the player to land on a wider variety of planets.

notes.title: Version 2.0 is Here!
notes.content:
Star Explorers just got Updated.  I have been making a lot of changes, and you'll know all about them if you are following the Beta version.  However, now all those changes have been updated into the Default version of Star Explorers.  

Here's  a summary of what you can expect:
[list]
[*]It looks like I've fixed the database issue, it has not shown itself in over two weeks of testing.  This was the biggest problem with the game, and it should be stable now.
[*]Main Mission works now.
[*]Landing Craft Beacon - press "B" to activate your beacon, so you can see where you landed on a planet.  
[*]New Aliens - you have to find them.
[*]Stackable Items - Gems, Quest Items, Ammo and other identical items will now "stack" when you collect them.  This way they no longer fill up your limited inventory slots.  
[*]Taking a screenshot no longer turns off the game's sound (use f12 to take screenshots and feel free to share what you find)
[*]Rare problem that caused the game to "forget" whether you were on a planet with acknexium fuel after reloading a game.
[*]New stylish H.U.D.
[*]New File Folder System - individual games are now stored in separate folders allowing for easier maintenance
[*]Memory Leaks Repaired
[*]Updated Textures - The game now uses DDS textures, which take up far less memory.
[*]More inspirational quotes on the loading screens - send me more if you find any good space quotes!
[/list]

You will have to start a new game if you have not been using the Beta version.  If you want to preserve your character's inventory, there is a way to do it.  Here are the steps you must take:

[list]
[*]Navigate to your game folder and find the "inventory_(name).txt" file - using "Properties>Local Files>Browse>Local Files"
[*]Copy and paste that file to your desktop.
[*]Uninstall Star Explorers
[*]Delete all the files remaining in the Star Explorers folder
[*]Reinstall Star Explorers
[*]Start a new game with the same name as the one on your "inventory_(name).txt" file.
[*]Play the game a bit, find a star system and save the game (you are no longer able to save games at the mothership)
[*]Exit the game
[*]Copy your inventory file, and paste it in the game folder with the same name
[*]Reload your game, and your inventory should be there!
[/list]

This is not the final version of the game, many changes and upgrades will continue to be added.  It is just a more stable platform on which to build these upcoming ideas.  Thanks for playing and for your ongoing patience!  I love the feedback I'm getting and I hope you all love to explore the stars!

notes.title: "Stackable Items"Update 07/17/2017
notes.content:
In this update - in the Beta Version - you will now be able to carry a lot more inventory because certain items are "stackable."  

[list]
[*]Gems, Ammo and quest artifacts gathered will no longer each take up a new inventory slot.  Instead, they will add to the quantity of an existing item of the same type.

[*]Selling stackable items includes an amount slider, so you can set the amount of each item you want to sell.  

[*]Fulfilling a quest for a particular item will reduce its quantity by one, instead of removing the whole stack.

[*]While armor upgrades are stackable, if they are sold, it will sell the whole stack.  (I'm working on making this work differently)

[*]Screenshots with f12 no longer turn off the game sounds.
[/list]

This should cut down on the number of times you have to return to the mothership, and make the game much more playable.  

NOTE: Items being picked up will look for the first open slot in your inventory.  If you have a certain kind of stackable item, then you drop or sell an item that occurs before that item in your inventory, then you pick up another one of those stackable items, it will fill in the open slot.  Until this is fixed, it can be remedied by dropping the second occurrence of the item, and picking it up again.

notes.title: Main Mission Working - Community Feedback Requested
notes.content:
I was able to run through the main mission with no crashes.  I still want o streamline it a bit, but it should be working now (in the beta version of the game).  

I plan to make this the default version after testing a bit more.  

Database issue seems resolved.  Main mission is working.  I will have my kids play over the weekend and set it to default as long as no more major issues show up.

With that said, I am considering this to be the first stable build of Star Explorers.  This is the place I SHOULD have been when I started Early Access, but I guess we live and learn.  

[h1]Feeback Request [/h1]
Where does everyone think I should go from here?  

I have several areas I plan to expand the game.  My question is not about what to do, but what order to do it in.  Here are the main areas I want to address:
[list]
[*]1. Streamlining the Game - As most reviewers have mentioned, Star Explorers is "rough around the edges."  I think this is most obvious in the way its menus work.  The somewhat confusing main mission and tutorial, and other things like how scanning things/picking up items does not always seem to work as expected.  It's clunky, and  I could spend quite some time getting the game to make more sense to new users and getting it to respond more smoothly.

[*]2. More Variety -  I plan to add lots of variety to the game environments.  Solar systems should have more than just planets, I am imagining moons, asteroids, maybe comets etc...  In between stars, there could also be giant nebulae, and maybe some strange anomalies that could pose a danger to the player.  Planets without life are kind of dull, so I want to add more variety of rocks and other terrain features.  Life bearing worlds all tend to look like earth outside of the color schemes.  I am picturing some very different kinds of plant and animal life.  Caves are all pretty much the same right now, so I plant to add more variety there too. 

[*]3. More Items - There are only a few different weapons and armor choices right now.  I plan to add more weapon types and more variety of weapon models for each type.  Armor might come in tiers, each tier having certain limits on how much damage it can absorb, for instance.  As the player progresses, more types of weapons and armor will become available.  I also want to add different utility items.  Some kind of scanning device, that will help navigate dangerous planets.  A portbale beacon that the player can set on a planet for future reference.  Some kind of climbing device, or maybe a jet pack.  Lots of ideas for items...

[*]4. Better Combat - Alien A.I. is pretty basic right now.  There are a few different types of aliens and each has a different set of approaches to the player.  Eventually, I want different alien types to interact with each other as well as with the player.  I also want to improve their combat skills and add drops for the player to find once they are defeated.  This is already true for the animal-like aliens, but it is missing from other types.  I also visualize the possibility of some kind of space combat with hostile aliens.

[*]5. More Quest Types - Currently there are only item retrieval quests available, whether from the mothership, or from friendly aliens.  Eventually, I want to add more options, like perhaps defeating an enemy, finding a location, defending an outpost, delivering things, etc... With even just a few different quest types, the gameplay could differ markedly from one game to another.
[/list]
Let me know which of these areas you'd like to see expanded in Star Explorers, or if there is something I'm missing that should be on the list.  As always, enjoy the game, and let me know if you find any problems or have any questions!

notes.title: New Beta Version Uploaded
notes.content:
[h1]Kinda Sorta Maybe Fixed It[/h1]
I uploaded the latest Beta for testing.  I don't want to make any bold declarations just yet, but after a couple hours of playing I did not encounter any database errors in this version.  

I found a piece of code in which the very files that were getting corrupted, were actually opened by the script, and under certain circumstances, were allowed to stay open.  By not closing these files, it was then easy for them to get corrupted.  I have made certain that these files do not remain open, and so far it seems to have corrected the problem, finally, but I am hesitant to say that I'm certain it's gone.  

[h1]More Testing Required[/h1]
I plan to test this version of the game over the next week or so before making it the default.  If you do decide to try it,  I recommend starting a new game.

If you want to preserve your old game, any existing database errors will still be there. 

Also, if you encounter the errors again, please let me know.  

[h1]Contingency Plan[/h1]
I have some more backup plans I can still implement in order to eliminate this issue.  

The next phase will be striping down the database script altogether.  I will make the database something that you start the game with.  This will remove the scanning process, and the map and star/planet info will just be fixed from the beginning.  I don't love this idea, but it's better than a corrupt database.  

Hopefully the script errors I found were the root cause and I won't have to resort to such drastic measures.

[h1]New Feature[/h1]
I forgot to mention another new feature of the Beta version of Star Explorers.  It is a behind the scenes issue, but I thought it should be mentioned.  The old version of the game simply saved all your files right there in the main folder.  This was messy and made it very difficult to delete a game if you wnated to do that.  

Now all user created files gets saved in a folder with the name you start the game with.  This makes it easier to identify, move, delete, and/or organize your saved game files.  If you go to the Star Explorers entry in your Steam Library, right click and select properties, then select "Browse Local Files" from the Local Files tab, you will be able to see the new folder structure.

notes.title: Update - Good News and Bad...
notes.content:
[h1]The Bad News[/h1]
I will give the bad news first.  The bad news is that the database corruption issue is still not resolved.  If I had known how challenging this was going to be to fix, I definitely would have delayed the release of this game, so I do apologize about the inconvenience.  

[h1]The Good News[/h1]
The good news (though it is only bittersweet due to the bad news already mentioned) is that I have uploaded a beta version of the game for testing.

This version of the game is accessible to interested players by right-clicking the Star Explorers icon/name in your game library and clicking on Properties.

Under the Betas tab, select "beta" from the drop down list, and the game should automatically update.

[h1]Features[/h1]
This newer version of the game does not look much different from the original, and, as mentioned above, still does not resolve the ongoing database issue.  However, it does have a new type of alien that you might run into on some planets.  

The landing craft has a "beacon" which you can activate using "b" when you are on a planet surface.  This makes it easier to find your way back, especially on those vapor planets.

Several memory leaks have detected and removed, as well as many textures that have been updated to dds format, which take up far less RAM.  The game starts at around 500 mb of RAM and while it does climb up, it also remains more stable than the older version.

notes.title: Major Update Underway
notes.content:
Thanks to some awesome players, I have gotten to the bottom of several of the remaining bugs.  I am also working on creating a more stable file structure for the game folder.  I am hoping that the next update will be the first truly stable version of the game. 

There is also a bunch of new content coming, which will be announced when the update is ready. 

In order to ensure player satisfaction as much as possible, I am planning on testing this next version quite extensively before putting it up on Steam.  This will take some time, but I want to make sure the game remains stable even after logging many hours of play time. 

As for the non-content updates, here is a list of what's to come:
[list]
[*]Main Quest - Currently, the main quest has some big problems.  You are better off simply going and exploring, and gathering resources for now.  These issues will be addressed, and you should be able to complete the main quest once the update is ready.  Currently, I believe it is possible to complete the main quest, but it can get messed up if you do things outside the main quest.  
[*]Stable Database - I am almost positive that I've finally gotten to the bottom of this insidious problem.  Previous "fixes" were simply patches that covered or put off the symptoms without addressing the root cause.  I believe I have found the source of the issue and it will be addressed in the update.  Rest assured I will be testing and tweaking this thoroughly before the update.
[*]File Structure - Having a coherent file structure will help in maintaining the program and user created files like the database.  Each new saved game will be in it's own separate folder, so there will be less clutter in the main game folder, and the game will be able to search for and access files more quickly, even after several ongoing saved games exist.  It will also help users to maintain their saved games either backing them up or transferring them, as all the pertinent data will be in one folder.
[*]Grass Goes Missing Issue - This was not a huge bug, and it was easy to fix once I realized what was happening.  In the current version, some of the grass and/or rocks on the planets will vanish.  This will stop happening in the update.
[*]Invisible Caves - Currently there is a bug that allows some planets to have invisible caves.  This means you may be walking on a terrain and suddenly the game will start loading a cave level, when there was not cave near you.  After leaving the cave you would end up at your spaceship, since the cave had no entrance.  This problem will be fixed in the update.
[*]Various smaller issues will be addressed and announced at the time of the update.
[*]Inventory Transfer - Since the update will be pretty major, you will have to start a new game to play it.  However, there will be a way to transfer your existing inventory into the new version, so don't feel like playing the game now will be a complete waste of time.  
[/list]

If I go quiet for a while, it means I am very busy testing and tweaking the game.  For the time being, please feel free to let me know what you think of Star Explorers, and how you think it could be improved.  I still want to have the final release ready by early 2018.  

For now, keep playing and sharing your discoveries on the Community Hub. The game is fairly stable and allows for exploration, combat, gathering of resources/equipment, upgrading your space-suit and more.  Only the database seems to be really unstable, so as long as you don't rely on it too much, you can still enjoy the game.

notes.title: Follow Up Update 05/28/2017
notes.content:
A quick patch of two outstanding issues:

[list]
[*]Bipedal Aliens Dialogue Issue - when commencing dialogue with friendly or neutral aliens, a bug was causing the alien to react as if it had been attacked.  They either died or began shooting/attacking the player.  Another related issue allowed the player to initiate dialogue with hostile aliens, causing the dialogue panel to remain open while the aliens attacked the player.  These should no longer occur.
[*]Ancient Ruins Reloading Issue - a bug was causing the ancient ruins to reload incorrectly upon returning to a planet, whether from the spaceship, or from a cave or the ruins themselves.  Ruins should now reload correctly - even if the planet was visited before this update.  
[*]Some Housecleaning - some functions were written is such a way as to be potential problems or memory leaks.  Some functions that run while aboard the spaceship for instance, would continue to run after landing on a planet, and vice-versa.  I have addressed several of these, making sure they are only running when they are supposed to be running.  
[/list]

Remember my goal is to get the game really stable and filled with more content for a full release next year.  Please feel free to provide specific feedback on what's wrong with the game and how you think it can be improved.  I am not waiting for feedback to actually make improvements though, I have a long list of things that need to be done, but I am certainly interested in what you, the players, have to say.  

Also, if you're not happy with the game right now, don't let that stop you from checking in to see the progress in a few weeks or so.  I plan to include more content on a weekly basis, along with fixing bugs and increasing the game's stability and streamlining its interface.

notes.title: Update 05-26-2017
notes.content:
Star Explorers has been updated!

This is a bigger update than previous ones, with new content and some bug fixes. 

First, a couple new features:
[list]
[*]Alien Ruins - Some planets may have the remnants of ancient alien cultures, with ruins to explore and in which to find rare items.  
[*]Dungeons - These anicient ruins may occasionally have cavernous dungeons to explore.  Similar to the existing caves, they are the beginning of adding more variety to the types of environments to explore.
[*]Planet Suns - This is not the finished product, but now you can see a little glowing sun up in the sky when on the surface of a planet.  This will be tweaked a lot in the next update, with different sizes and colors depending on the sun's parameters.  
[/list]
Fixes:
[list]
[*]Shadows Flickering Issue - The shadows on planet surfaces were flickering.  I have spent a lot of time figuring out how to remove this issue, and I think it is successful.  There are still a couple of planet objects that will show the flickering shadow problem, namely the landing craft and any stray treasure chests you find.  However other objects like trees, rocks and ancient ruins should no longer cause this problem.
[*]Landscape Density and Intrusion - Landscape items occasionally created problems by appearing over cave entrances, or intersecting the player's landing craft.  This issue should be resolved now, and landscape object density has beed reduced a bit.
[/list]

As with previous updates, your existing games *should not* be effected.  I hope they are not, but let me know if you experience any issues.  Any planets you visited before the new features will remain unchanged, but new planets will have a chance to exhibit the new ancient ruin features.  The shadow flickering issue should be resolved regardless of which planet you visit.  

In other news, I found out that the "Star Missing from Database" issue is not quite gone yet.  Reducing the number of stars that form in each sector helped prevent this in some cases, but there are other possible causes for this.  I am closing in on the causes, and I will ask anyone who encounters this to consider helping me out by sending me a file from their local Star Explorers folder.  I will write an explanation of what to do in the Discussions Tab.

notes.title: Small but Important Update
notes.content:
I believe I have fixed one of the big bugs, along with one minor issue...

[list]
[*]The star chart was getting messed up because certain sectors of the galaxy were being generated with more stars than the database could handle.  This resulted in issues like not being able to scan planets after returning to your ship.  It also may have been responsible for the "invalid" pointer issue that some people encountered (though I have not actually encountered this issue, so we'll see)
[*]Invisible cave monsters.  There was a problem in the code that caused certain aliens to be invisible in some of the cave systems.  This should not happen any more.  
[/list]

I do have another, content rich, update coming soon.  I would have waited to release this update with that one, but the Star Chart issue will cause problems even in current games if you started the game before this update.  If you want to avoid this issue altogether, you will probably want to start a new game.  Feel free to continue your existing games if you don't mind the database getting messed up though, it *should* not effect other aspects of the game.

notes.title: Update
notes.content:
Star Explorers has received its first update.  It's nothing huge, but more of a preliminary, housekeeping kind of update.  Here are the issues that have been addressed:

[list]
[*]A simple in-game tutorial has been added.  Nothing fancy, but when you are receiving messages from the mothership, there is a second tutorial section which gives practical advice on how to accomplish the tasks.
[*]Configuration changes are now saved in separate file and loaded each time you play automatically.  Now you will only have to set up your screen, mouse configuration and volume levels once.  The changes will be carried over into your next play session automatically.
[*]The Sector Cube is now more versatile - This cube existed and showed the boundaries of the sector in which the player's spaceship resided.  Now, it will appear not only in the player's current sector, but in any sector the player chooses in the star chart.  Also, by clicking "target sector" in the star chart, the sector cube will be automaticlaly repositioned on the sector in which the player must complete the current mission.  You can still toggle its visibility with "O" or by ckicking the "show/hide" button in the star chart.
[*]More screen sizes have been added. [b]NOTE: some of these are untested.  Annything over 1920 x 1080 is too big for my monitor.  Also, I had an error when trying to use 1680 x 1050 at full screen.[/b] 
[*]Cursor should be released when you press "esc" allowing you to use the mouse in other Windows programs while Star Explorers is running.
[*]Mouse Sensitivity Slider added to the "Options > Controls" panel.
[*]Mouse Invert Y Axis option added to the "Options > Controls" panel.
[*]Unsaved Games - Previously, if you started a new game, but forgot to save it, or had not yet successfully returned from a planet, the game would not load again.  Now it should automatically save your game right after creating it, so even if you turn it off before landing on a planet, you'll still be able to reload the game.
[*]Checks previously saved games - Now if you accidently type an existing game's name into the "New Game" window, it will check to see if that game exists already or not.  Starting a new game with an existing name would have caused lots of errors.  This should not happen any more.
[*]New surface features - The first of many new planet features has been added.  Now some planets will have what I call "landscape features" which are essentially just big rocks.  Nevertheless, they give a more unique appearance to each planet, allowing for more variety.  Some aspects of these features still need tweaking, as aliens might go right through them, and shadows seem to have a problem of flickering on their large surfaces.  I am working on these issues and will hopefully correct them by the next update.
[*]Compatible with the original release of Star Explorers.  All these new features SHOULD work flawlessly with any saved games you may have.
[/list]

Thanks for keeping up with the development of Star Explorers, and as always, let me know if you have any questions or concerns!

notes.title: Did You Know?
notes.content:
Did you know you can do the following?
[list]
[*]Refill your air tank, along with suit and health at the landing craft.  Just approach the back-hatch, as you would when departing from a planet, and hold your mouse so the small hand icon appears.  If you just stay there, without pressing "E," your air tank will beging refilling.  - It also refills your suit and health, but I have plans to change this, so don't get used to it.  Health packs and suit repair kits, and perhaps a repair/health station in your ship.
[*]Find treasures in caves.  Some caves have more than just crystals.  Sometimes aliens land on planets to use them as storage facilities.  You may stumble across a hidded cache of weapons, armor or other items deep inside a planet's cave system.
[*]Survive on hazardous planets.  If you act quickly enough, you may be able to risk a little pain and difficulty in exchange for important resources.  Landing on a hazardous planet is not usually advisable, but in a pinch, doing so may get you the fuel crystals or other resources you need.  Just be careful you don't waste too much time down there!
[/list]
Please feel free to share any other tips you may have come across in your efforts.

[*]Find treasures in caves.  Some caves have more than just crystals.  Sometimes aliens land on planets to use them as storage facilities.  You may stumble across a hidded cache of weapons, armor or other items deep inside a planet's cave system.
[*]Survive on hazardous planets.  If you act quickly enough, you may be able to risk a little pain and difficulty in exchange for important resources.  Landing on a hazardous planet is not usually advisable, but in a pinch, doing so may get you the fuel crystals or other resources you need.  Just be careful you don't waste too much time down there!
[/list]
Please feel free to share any other tips you may have come across in your efforts.

notes.title: Early Access Release
notes.content:
As most of you probably know, the official Early Access release of Star Explorers happened Monday morning.

http://store.steampowered.com/app/502720/Star_Explorers/

I'd like to say thanks to everyone who voted for it on Greenlight, and continue to show support by providing valuable feedback on the current build of the game.

Of course, being Early Access means the game is not finished, and even has some big bugs in it.  It is my hope, that with your help, I can quickly track down the remaining bugs and squash them flat.  I also want to hear what you all think about the game-play.  What's good ... what's bad ... what's missing altogether?

For now, I am assembling a priority to-do list.  

Here is what I'm hearing from current players:
[list]
[*]Have some kind of in-game tutorial.  The controls are difficult and not obvious to new players. I agree.  Streamlining the gameplay and UI are my top priority at this point.  For now, please refer to the "How to Play" guide on the main store page, and check the "Options > Controls" panel in-game for reference.
[*]Full Screen doesn't work, or stops working.  I did test it, and I did not have errors, but that's why having more people involved helps.  For now, you will only be able to change screen resolution or switch to full screen from the main start menu.  Once you begin playing, you won't have access to video options.  I will definitely be adding a feature that saves your configuration as default.  
[*]Crash or Error on Scanning Planets.  I knew about this one, but could not always reproduce it, so it was hard to test.  Thankfully, a user has identified where and when it happens, so I should be able to get rid of it quickly.
[*]Option to invert mouse y axis.  I never play games like this, but I'm happy to oblige.
[*]Mouse Sensitivity.  Some people are having issues with mouse sensitivity.  I will add a slider in the Options menu ASAP.
[*]So far, no one has reported the missing inventory error.  This is good ,I may have fixed it.  However, I did encounter a problem when switching out my space suit.  It was resolved, and no data went missing, but there was a moment when the new space suit disappeared, and seemed lost.  I have included a small script that displays a warning if and when you remove your space suit or main weapon.  If this alert pops up at any point, where you did not actually unequip these items, please let me know.
[/list]

In a few days I will be back at programming, I will do my best to implement these and more fixes as soon as I can.  I estimate the first update in about two weeks.  After that I hope to update more regularly.  If my calculations are correct, updates should not effect saved games, and you will be able to resume your ongoing games after updates are installed.  

Of course I have a long list of minor fixes and another long list of features I want to add to the game before the full release.  As mentioned in the Early Access description, I think I can accomplish all these things in one year's time.
